nodes.description: External view function that derives a pseudo-random number from tx.origin, nonce, blockhash of previous block, block.timestamp and seed, then applies modulo mod.
Attacker-controllable origin address fed into the keccak256 randomness preimage.
Miner/validator-influenceable timestamp used in the randomness preimage, making the result predictable/dependent on block conditions.
Weak randomness generation: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(tx.origin, nonce, blockhash(block.number - 1), block.timestamp, seed)) is fully predictable and manipulable by callers and block producers.
Modulo operation using a caller-supplied divisor mod; a zero mod causes a division-by-zero revert (Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic).
Caller-supplied seed mixed into the randomness preimage of randomMod.
Caller-supplied nonce mixed into the randomness preimage of randomMod.
Caller-supplied modulus acting as the divisor of the keccak256 output in randomMod.

edges.reason: tx.origin is read inside randomMod and becomes part of the returned randomness value, creating origin/identity dependency.
block.timestamp is read inside randomMod and becomes part of the returned randomness value, creating timestamp dependency.
The seed parameter is passed into randomMod and encoded into the keccak256 preimage.
The nonce parameter is passed into randomMod and encoded into the keccak256 preimage.
The mod parameter is passed into randomMod and used as the modulus of the returned value.
tx.origin flows directly into the keccak256 randomness preimage, letting the caller influence the generated number.
block.timestamp flows directly into the keccak256 randomness preimage, letting block producers influence the generated number.
seed is packed into abi.encodePacked for the keccak256 randomness preimage.
nonce is packed into abi.encodePacked for the keccak256 randomness preimage.
randomMod executes the weak keccak256 randomness computation as its core logic before returning.
randomMod applies the modulo arithmetic operation on the keccak256 result using the caller-supplied mod.
The caller-supplied mod parameter is the divisor of the modulo operation, so mod == 0 triggers an arithmetic revert.

normalization_plan.reason: seed is a call-scoped parameter whose only role is being consumed by the randomMod randomness computation, so it collapses into the function node.
nonce is a call-scoped parameter used only inside randomMod's keccak256 preimage, so it collapses into the function node.
mod directly parameterizes the modulo divisor, so it collapses into the modulo unsafe_operation node.
